# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 43 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 43 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_043_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 11, Part 2 — Further Signs of True and False Prophets

**43:1** "Hear then both the spirit of the divine and the spirit of earthly origin. Discern each by the works. Trust the spirit of divinity when it comes from above, from the power of God; but the earthly spirit has no power and is empty and foolish."

**43:2** "First, concerning the man who seems to have the Spirit: he who is exalted and wishes to take the first seat and is bold and shameless and talkative and lives in luxury and among many other deceptions — and he takes payment for his prophesying, and if he does not receive payment he does not prophesy — can the Spirit of God take payment for prophesying? It is not possible for a prophet of God to do this. But the spirit of such prophets is earthly."

**43:3** "Then again, look at the life of the man who has the divine Spirit. The man who has the Spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble and keeps away from all wickedness and vain desire of this world, and makes himself more lowly than all men, and answers no one when asked, and speaks not by himself alone — for the Holy Spirit does not speak when man wishes to speak, but the Spirit speaks at the time when God wishes him to speak."

**43:4** "When therefore the man who has the divine Spirit comes into an assembly of righteous men who have faith in the Holy Spirit, and prayer is made, the man is filled with the Holy Spirit and speaks to the congregation as God wills. Thus the Spirit of God will be manifest. Such therefore is the power of the Lord's Spirit."

**43:5** "Listen now concerning the earthly and empty spirit, which has no power but is foolish. First, that man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wishes to have the first place, and he is bold and shameless and talkative and accustomed to luxury and to many other deceptions, and he accepts payment for his divination. When you see such a man, keep away from him."

**43:6** "Now hear again concerning the true prophet: the man who has the divine Spirit does not exalt himself nor desires to speak first. Neither does he live in luxury, nor does he inquire about anything by means of money — but if anyone inquires of him, he answers not by himself, but rather by the will of God. And since the Holy Spirit of God himself rests upon this man, he will speak the things that the Lord commands."

**43:7** "When therefore both spirits come together into one place, and if you wish, through prayer for discernment, to test which is the true and which the false — hear. Test the man who has the divine Spirit through life. First, the one who has the divine Spirit from God — test him in life. See whether the life of the man who has the spirit is consistent with upright life."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the community discernment framework of Hermas.*
